sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205].
The path was a step change, not a smooth climb: revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021, then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in the last three years [D183][D230][D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores [P51], and FY2025's decline reflected a 2.6% comparable sales decrease driven by 2.2% lower traffic [P14].
Operating income compounded at only 0.6% over the window against 4.5% revenue growth, so the ten-year record is one of volume growth without profit leverage [F207][F205].
Merchandise sales are 98.0% of revenue and fell 2.0% in FY2025, contributing -2.0pp to the total decline [D465][D466][D467].
Food & beverage grew 1.3% in FY2025 and now makes up 23.0% of revenue, up from 19.6% in FY2017, while apparel fell 4.7% and home furnishings fell to $15.6 billion [D507][D506][D484][D564][S33].
The filings attribute the discretionary weakness to sales declines across Apparel & Accessories, Hardlines and Home Furnishings & Decor, partly offset by Frequency categories [P30].
Profit did not grow with revenue: operating income fell 8.1% in FY2025 against a 1.7% revenue decline, and revenue growth trailed operating-cost growth by 0.4pp [D417][D416][D439].
Diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% net income growth because the diluted share count fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [F210][F208][X107][X116].
The FY2025 operating margin of 4.9% sits below the 5.6% window median and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high, though above the 3.5% FY2022 low [F34][D590][D589][D588].
The latest 0.3pp decline came almost entirely from cost of revenue, which added -0.3pp, while SG&A added +0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The gross margin rate fell to 27.9% from 28.2%, and the filing attributes the decrease to the net impact of several items it does not quantify [P12].
The SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because of a 0.6pp benefit from interchange fee settlements; excluding it, the adjusted rate rose to 20.9% on sales deleveraging [P11].
Below the line, the 22.3% effective tax rate and $445 million interest expense left net margin 1.3pp under operating margin [D403][X66][D629].

Operating cash flow of $6.56 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.01x window median, and free cash flow of $2.84 billion was 0.77x net income against a 1.01x median [F84][F44][D404][D619][F104][D405][D599].
The operating cash flow decline reflects lower net earnings and the net impact of lower accounts payable leverage and inventory purchases [P7].
Free cash flow margin fell to 2.7% from 4.2%, below the 4.5% window median and the 4.2% retail peer median [D401][D355][D596][D611].
Capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion, 3.6% of revenue and 1.19x D&A, reflecting increased investment in new stores and remodels [D423][F94][D400][D406][P5].
Cash was $5.49 billion against $14.4 billion of long-term debt in FY2025, a net debt position, with a current ratio of 0.94x [F144][F194][F184].
The current ratio matches the 0.94x window median but sits below the 1.03x FY2020 high, and return on average equity of 24.0% trails the 28.6% retail peer median [F184][D602][D601][D415][D617].
Free cash flow covered buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion at 86.8%, with repurchases cut to $408 million from $7.36 billion in FY2021 [D412][D413][X126][X122].
The diluted share count fell 1.3% in FY2025 and 21.8% over the window, which is why EPS growth outran net income growth [D434][X107][X116].
Revenue has now fallen three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025, a 1.3% three-year CAGR [F7][F10][D603][R1].
The decline is traffic-led, with comparable sales down 2.6% on a 2.2% traffic decrease, so the top line is shrinking before price or mix help [P14].
The current ratio of 0.94x is below 1.0x, meaning current liabilities of $21.2 billion exceed current assets of $20.0 billion [F184][F164][F154][R2].
Operating margin has slipped two years in a row, 0.4pp in total, to 4.9%, and free cash flow fell 36.7% in FY2025 [F32][F33][F34][R4][D422].

Two data breaks affect comparisons: short-term investments are already inside cash, and the current portion of debt was inside long-term debt in FY2016-FY2018, so net cash and debt growth are not used here [R7][R8].
Whether revenue stops falling: a fourth decline would extend the streak, while a return above the FY2025 $104.8 billion level would break it [F10][R1].
Whether the operating margin recovers toward the 5.6% window median from 4.9%, or slips toward the 3.5% FY2022 low [D590][F34][D588].
Whether capex stays near the roughly $5 billion FY2026 guidance, which would keep free cash flow margin under the 4.5% median if operating cash flow does not recover [P4][D596].
